caption:
Earth is 4.5 billion years old. This planet is not even 1 million.
Astrophysical Journal Letters, 16 Sept 2026. Bernardi, Cieza and colleagues, Universidad Diego Portales.

Elias 2-24 b is the youngest planet ever found: under 1 million years old, roughly Jupiter's mass (models give about 2 to 4), about 450 light-years away and still embedded in its disk, about 55 au from its star. Found in archival Keck data by a Universidad Diego Portales team led by Andrea Bernardi. Astrophysical Journal Letters, 16 Sept 2026.

#space #astronomy #exoplanet #science
voiceover_script: Earth is four and a half billion years old. This planet is not even one million. It is called Elias 2-24 b, and it is the youngest planet ever found. The previous record holders are all over five million years old. It is roughly Jupiter's mass, though the models give anything from about two to four Jupiters. It sits about four hundred and fifty light-years away, still embedded in the disk of material it formed from, about fifty five astronomical units out from its star. Nobody pointed a new telescope at it. The team, led by Andrea Bernardi at Universidad Diego Portales, found it in archival data from the Keck Observatory.
